description: The unit (macos-latest) job runs the whole unit suite in one job, a median of 6 to 7 minutes and up to 9.5 minutes, against about 3 minutes for the ubuntu leg on the same heads, so it sets the wall-clock time of the whole pipeline and of every review round that waits for it.
goal: Split the unit suite of the macOS leg of .github/workflows/test-unit.yml into two parallel shards, each running a stable, deterministic half of the unit test files chosen by a new script scripts/unit_test_shard.py (a pure function mapping a test file path and a shard count to a shard index by a stable hash, and a command-line mode that prints the test files of one shard from a pytest collection), so no test file runs twice and none is skipped. The ubuntu leg keeps running the whole suite in one job. The CI timing gate, the timing record upload and the macOS relevance gate keep working for each shard, with the shard in the record and job names so baselines are compared like for like. Code is self-explaining: no docstrings and no comments except '# why:' comments that record a reason the code cannot show.
rationale: Halving the longest job shortens every pipeline wait by several minutes, which is the largest remaining wall-clock cost of every flow.
acceptance_criteria: Bring the pipeline's wall-clock time down by sharding the unit suite.

A test in apps/sandbox-executor/tests/test_unit_test_shard.py runs scripts/unit_test_shard.py on the real list of unit test files collected from this repository for 2 shards and asserts every file lands in exactly one shard, the two shards together equal the full set, and each shard holds between 40 and 60 percent of the files.
The same test file asserts the shard of a file does not change when unrelated files are added to the list.

A test in the same file reads .github/workflows/test-unit.yml and asserts the macOS leg runs two shards through scripts/unit_test_shard.py, the ubuntu leg runs the whole suite, and the timing gate step passes the shard so records and baselines are per shard.
`unit (macos-latest)` run time on code heads is below its 7.0 min median, by dependency and image caching, sharding the unit suite, or both, with the measured result stated.
All tests pass via 'uv run pytest' and 'uv run task lint' passes.
